description: 220 is a bidding variant of Twenty-Five, Ireland's national card game. Players bid and play tricks; each trick is worth 5 points. First side to reach 220 points wins. Uses standard 52-card deck, 5 cards each, next card for trump. Trump order: 5, J, A, K, Q, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 4, 3, 2; Ace of Hearts is always trump.

content.text: 220 is a bidding variant of Twenty-Five, Ireland's national card game. Players bid and play tricks; each trick is worth 5 points. First side to reach 220 points wins. Uses standard 52-card deck, 5 cards each, next card for trump. Trump order: 5, J, A, K, Q, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 4, 3, 2; Ace of Hearts is always trump.

220 is the highest-target bidding variant in Ireland's national card game family. Twenty-Five (25) is descended from the Scottish game Maw and from Five Cards described by Charles Cotton in 1674; it resurfaced in the 19th century as Spoil Five and Forty-Five. The bidding games 55, 110 and 220 use the same rules as 25 but with a round of bidding and a kitty; the only difference is the target score (55, 110 or 220 points). 220 is played over many deals until one player or team first reaches 220 points.
Standard 52-card French pack. One pack; five cards to each player and five to the kitty. No jokers.
5 cards each; next card turned for trump.

items.text: Shared bidding variations: Groups may apply the same bidding variants described for 55 and 110 (such as only the bidder being able to win, or naming trump before seeing the kitty) when playing to a 220-point target.
